svg.title: Project baseline, the SDLC cycle and supporting expertise
svg.desc: The project baseline contains accepted decisions, working conventions and reproducible foundations. Read it as input to relevant work across product direction, development and feedback; establish missing foundations after sufficient decisions and update the baseline as the project evolves. Shared methods and matching technical expertise support the flow rather than form additional lifecycle stages. Technical guidance informs feasibility and requirements and applies through design, implementation, testing, delivery and maintenance; select it for the accepted stack. Connecting rails point into all three parts of the flow. Product discovery and priorities feed planning, with business strategy supporting unresolved business direction. The SDLC cycles through planning, requirements analysis, design, implementation, testing, deployment and maintenance. Testing loops back to implementation for repair and rechecking. Design includes architecture, experience, visual direction and contracts. Detailed implementation planning follows those decisions. Live product feedback informs discovery and the next development cycle; evidence can reopen any affected decision. Each card explains its purpose in plain language; Green filled labels show skills as direct requests; red outlined labels show skills supporting requested work. Neutral labels name project records. These indicate usage in this diagram, not exclusive skill types; a skill can serve both roles. A visible legend and distinct filled versus dashed-outline styles accompany the colors. Planning uses product-management for goals and priorities; refine owns detailed requirements, and plan sequences implementation after design. Skills shown are representative; research, explicit clarification, documentation, Git, security, reliability and observability support discovery, development and feedback.
